---
name: CI

# Path-filtered SIMT lane: skip when a change cannot affect cuda-oxide or the
# shared host crates. `cuda-oxide/**` is deliberately broad (prose as well as
# code) because guard scripts cross-check the book against the crates.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'cuda-oxide/**'
      - 'cuda-bindings/**'
      - 'cuda-core/**'
      - 'cuda-core-derive/**'
      - 'cuda-async/**'
      - 'Cargo.toml'
      - 'Cargo.lock'
      - '.github/workflows/**'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'cuda-oxide/**'
      - 'cuda-bindings/**'
      - 'cuda-core/**'
      - 'cuda-core-derive/**'
      - 'cuda-async/**'
      - 'Cargo.toml'
      - 'Cargo.lock'
      - '.github/workflows/**'

concurrency:
  group: ci-gate-${{ github.ref_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# Every other workflow in the repo pins this rather than inheriting whatever the
# repository default happens to be. This one is a pure caller today, so the four
# called workflows' own `contents: read` already bounds the token and this
# changes nothing. It matters for the next job added here directly: a `uses:`
# job carries the callee's permissions, an inline `steps:` job would carry the
# default instead, and that difference is invisible in review.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  fmt:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/fmt.yml

  clippy:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/clippy.yml

  unit-tests:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/unit-tests.yml

  cargo-deny:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/cargo-deny.yml

---
name: unit-tests

# Runs as a job of the top-level CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml),
# which is the single push/pull_request entry point. Concurrency is governed
# by CI's own group, so this workflow declares none of its own.
on:
  workflow_call:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  rust-unit-tests:
    name: cargo test -p ${{ matrix.package }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # Each entry must be runnable on a stock `ubuntu-latest` runner — i.e.
        # no live GPU. `needs_cuda: true` installs the CUDA toolkit for build-
        # time bindgen (every crate that transitively depends on
        # `cuda-bindings` needs `cuda.h` to compile). `test_args` overrides
        # the default `--all-targets` where a crate needs a narrower set.
        #
        # Crates intentionally not in this matrix:
        #   * `fuzzer` — differential-testing infra with no unit tests.
        #   * `rustc-codegen-cuda` — its own [workspace] that links against
        #     `rustc-private` dylibs; covered by the separate job below.
        #
        # Everything else is here on purpose. This list is the whole
        # justification for a member being absent, so a member that is neither
        # in the matrix below nor named above is an omission, not a decision —
        # which is how `dialect-iket`, `iket-lower`, `dialect-ptx` and
        # `ptx-parse` came to carry 107 tests that no CI job ran.
        include:
          # In-kernel event tracing: the semantic dialect and its lowering to a
          # runtime compatibility profile. Pure pliron, no CUDA.
          - package: dialect-iket
          - package: iket-lower
          # The PTX stack from #914-#917: a lossless CST over PTX source and the
          # structured dialect projected from it. Pure Rust, no CUDA, and the
          # dialect's CFG verification is exactly the kind of invariant a unit
          # test is the only cheap way to keep.
          - package: ptx-parse
          - package: dialect-ptx
          # Schedule-perturbation campaigns over that PTX stack: seeded
          # nanosleep injection plus run classification. Pure Rust, no CUDA.
          - package: ptx-schedule
          - package: cuda-intrinsics-gen
          - package: cuda-target-spec
          - package: cuda-intrinsics
          - package: llvm-export
          - package: dialect-mir
          - package: dialect-nvvm
          - package: mir-importer
          # Includes a real llc -> ptxas spine-kernel validation.
          - package: cuda-oxide-codegen
            needs_cuda: true
          - package: mir-lower
          - package: mir-transforms
          - package: nvvm-transforms
          # `default = []`, but every consumer turns the object features on:
          # rustc-codegen-cuda takes `object-write`, and the shared cuda-core
          # (cutile-rs, via its crates.io oxide-artifacts) takes `object-read`.
          # Testing the default set alone skips the eight ELF emit/extract
          # tests that cover the configuration actually built.
          - package: oxide-artifacts
            test_args: --all-targets --features object
          - package: reserved-oxide-symbols
          # launch_requires_unsafe trybuild fixture dev-depends on
          # cuda-host/cuda-core, which transitively pull cuda-bindings
          - package: cuda-macros
            needs_cuda: true
          # trybuild compile-fail suite for ThreadIndex / DisjointSlice safety
          - package: cuda-device
          # Runtime CUDA compiler/linker discovery and file-identity checks;
          # live-toolkit tests remain explicitly ignored on stock runners.
          - package: libnvvm-sys
          - package: nvjitlink-sys
          # Driverless shared libNVVM/nvJitLink policy. Its default suite is
          # pure and validates options, provenance, and cubin structure; the
          # live-toolkit smoke test remains explicitly ignored.
          - package: cuda-artifact-finalizer
          # pure-Rust kernel-launch helpers + tcgen05 tiling tables
          - package: cuda-host
            needs_cuda: true
          # cargo subcommand wrapper; pure Rust, no CUDA toolkit required.
          # Running it on a runner with NO toolkit installed is the
          # regression gate for issue #87.
          - package: cargo-oxide

    steps:
      - name: Clone repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install CUDA toolkit
        if: matrix.needs_cuda
        uses: Jimver/cuda-toolkit@v0.2.35
        id: cuda-toolkit
        with:
          cuda: "13.1.1"
          method: network
          sub-packages: '["nvcc", "cudart-dev"]'
          non-cuda-sub-packages: '["libcurand-dev"]'

      - name: Install LLVM 21 (llc/opt for the NVPTX backend)
        if: matrix.package == 'cuda-oxide-codegen'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source /etc/os-release
          sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings
          wget -qO- https://apt.llvm.org/llvm-snapshot.gpg.key \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/keyrings/apt-llvm-org.asc >/dev/null
          echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/apt-llvm-org.asc] https://apt.llvm.org/${VERSION_CODENAME}/ llvm-toolchain-${VERSION_CODENAME}-21 main" \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/llvm-21.list
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends llvm-21
          llc-21 --version | head -2
          opt-21 --version | head -2

      - name: Run crate unit tests
        env:
          CUDA_TOOLKIT_PATH: ${{ steps.cuda-toolkit.outputs.CUDA_PATH }}
        working-directory: cuda-oxide
        run: |
          sysroot="$(rustc --print sysroot)"
          export LIBRARY_PATH="${sysroot}/lib:${LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
          export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${sysroot}/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"

          # No libcuda shadowing: the shared cuda-bindings (cutile-rs) loads
          # libcuda at run time through libloading, so test binaries carry no
          # DT_NEEDED on `libcuda.so.1` and load on a driverless runner. The
          # tests that need a real driver are `#[ignore]`d.
          cargo test -p ${{ matrix.package }} ${{ matrix.test_args || '--all-targets' }}

      # End-to-end proof for issue #87: on this runner there is no CUDA
      # toolkit and no driver, yet doctor must build, load, and reach its
      # checks (it exits 1 here because nvcc/cuda.h are missing, which is
      # exactly the diagnosis it exists to print).
      - name: cargo oxide doctor reaches its checks without the CUDA toolkit
        if: matrix.package == 'cargo-oxide'
        working-directory: cuda-oxide
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          out="$(cargo run -p cargo-oxide -- doctor 2>&1)" || true
          printf '%s\n' "${out}"
          printf '%s\n' "${out}" | grep -q "CUDA headers (cuda.h)"

  rustc-codegen-cuda-unit-tests:
    name: cargo test --lib (rustc-codegen-cuda)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Clone repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # This standalone workspace uses rustc-private APIs, so run its tests
      # directly rather than pretending the root package matrix covers them.
      # The live CUDA-tool tests remain ignored; these regressions need no GPU
      # or toolkit installation.
      - name: Run codegen-backend unit tests
        working-directory: cuda-oxide/crates/rustc-codegen-cuda
        run: |
          sysroot="$(rustc --print sysroot)"
          export LIBRARY_PATH="${sysroot}/lib:${LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
          export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${sysroot}/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
          cargo test --lib

  generated-intrinsics:
    name: generated intrinsics are current and ABI-compatible
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Clone repository with ABI history
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      # cuda-intrinsics-gen shells out to rustfmt when it writes generated
      # sources; it comes from rust-toolchain.toml's component list.

      - name: Check generated intrinsic outputs
        working-directory: cuda-oxide
        run: cargo run -p cuda-intrinsics-gen -- check

      - name: Probe every declared LLVM-NVPTX target
        working-directory: cuda-oxide
        run: |
          # Stock runners do not carry the recorded CUDA 13.3 ptxas binary.
          # Identity is llc version plus the rustc commit from upstream.lock;
          # binary bytes are provenance only.
          cargo run -p cuda-intrinsics-gen -- probe --all --skip-terminal --per-target

      - name: Check append-only intrinsic ABI ledger
        working-directory: cuda-oxide
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
            base_ref="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          else
            before="${{ github.event.before }}"
            zero="0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"
            if [ -n "${before}" ] && [ "${before}" != "${zero}" ] && git cat-file -e "${before}^{commit}"; then
              base_ref="${before}"
            elif git rev-parse --verify HEAD^ >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              base_ref="HEAD^"
            else
              base_ref="HEAD"
            fi
          fi
          cargo run -p cuda-intrinsics-gen -- check-abi-history --base-ref "${base_ref}"

[package]
name = "cuda-target-spec"
version = "0.1.0"
edition.workspace = true
authors.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
repository.workspace = true
description = "Shared CUDA target parsing and recorded LLVM PTX-floor policy"
readme = "README.md"

[dependencies]

[package]
name = "mathdx_ffi_test"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
authors = ["Nihal Pasham <nihalp@nvidia.com>"]
license = "Apache-2.0"

[workspace]

[dependencies]
cuda-device = { path = "../../../cuda-device" }
cuda-host = { path = "../../../cuda-host" }
cuda-core = { path = "../../../../../cuda-core", version = "0.4.0" }

# For runtime LTOIR generation (Option B) - optional
libmathdx-sys = { path = "libmathdx-sys", optional = true }

[features]
default = []
# Enable libmathdx-based LTOIR generation (Option B)
# Requires LIBMATHDX_PATH environment variable to be set
libmathdx = ["dep:libmathdx-sys"]

[package]
name = "difftest"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"

# See more keys and their definitions at https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html

[dependencies]
config = { path = "../config" }
clap = "4.1.4"
colored = "2.0.0"
env_logger = "0.11.3"
log = "0.4.17"
rayon = "1.7.0"
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
tempfile = "3.3.0"

# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

# Fixture for scripts/check-device-only-build.sh. Not a workspace member: the
# point is a graph that does NOT contain cuda-host, so it must resolve on its
# own rather than share the SIMT workspace's lockfile and dependency set.
[package]
name = "device-only-kernels"
version = "0.0.0"
edition = "2024"
license = "Apache-2.0"
publish = false

[workspace]

[dependencies]
cuda-device = { path = "../../../cuda-device" }
# `default-features = false` drops the `host` feature, and with it every
# `::cuda_host` / `::cuda_core` path the macros would otherwise emit. That is
# the whole subject of this fixture; adding cuda-host here would defeat it.
cuda-macros = { path = "../..", default-features = false }

[package]
name = "small_type_ffi_test"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
authors = ["Nihal Pasham <nihalp@nvidia.com>"]
license = "Apache-2.0"

[workspace]

[dependencies]
cuda-device = { path = "../../../cuda-device" }
cuda-host = { path = "../../../cuda-host" }
cuda-core = { path = "../../../../../cuda-core", version = "0.4.0" }

[package]
name = "device_ffi_test"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
authors = ["Nihal Pasham <nihalp@nvidia.com>"]
license = "Apache-2.0"

[workspace]

[dependencies]
cuda-device = { path = "../../../cuda-device" }
cuda-host = { path = "../../../cuda-host" }
cuda-core = { path = "../../../../../cuda-core", version = "0.4.0" }

[package]
name = "cast_tests"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
authors = ["Nihal Pasham <nihalp@nvidia.com>"]
license = "Apache-2.0"

[workspace]

[dependencies]
cuda-device = { path = "../../../cuda-device" }
cuda-host = { path = "../../../cuda-host" }
cuda-core = { path = "../../../../../cuda-core", version = "0.4.0" }

[package]
name = "mcast_barrier_test"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
license = "Apache-2.0"

[workspace]

# Minimal test for mbarrier_arrive_cluster + try_wait_parity in a loop.
# Tests the MCAST_BAR protocol used in gemm_sol_clc for TMA multicast.
# Build with:
#   cargo oxide run mcast_barrier_test

[dependencies]
cuda-device = { path = "../../../cuda-device" }
cuda-host = { path = "../../../cuda-host" }
cuda-core = { path = "../../../../../cuda-core", version = "0.4.0" }

[package]
name = "libmathdx-sys"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
description = "Raw FFI bindings to NVIDIA libmathdx (runtime code-generation for MathDx)"
authors = ["Nihal Pasham <nihalp@nvidia.com>"]
license = "Apache-2.0"
repository = "https://github.com/NVlabs/cuda-oxide.git"
keywords = ["cuda", "ffi", "nvidia", "mathdx", "fft", "blas"]
categories = ["external-ffi-bindings", "science"]

[build-dependencies]
bindgen = "0.72.1"

[dependencies]

[features]
default = []

# Reviewed special-register reads that already have stable cuda-device APIs.

schema = 32
family = "sreg"

[special_registers]
llvm_evidence_profile = "rust-llvm-23.1.0-16696adc"
libnvvm_evidence_profile = "cuda-13.3-libnvvm-13.3.33"
runtime_validation = "unexecuted"
registers = [
    "clock",
    "clock64",
    "globaltimer",
    "envreg1",
    "envreg2",
    "smid",
    "nsmid",
    "gridid",
    "warpid",
    "nwarpid",
    "dynamic_smem_size",
    "total_smem_size",
]
product_count = 12
